subject: Science
chapter: Topic-based: use with whichever Class 9 book your students follow
title: Quick Revision: The Fundamental Unit of Life (Cell)

bullets: Robert Hooke (1665) saw cells in a thin slice of cork. Leeuwenhoek first saw free-living cells in pond water. Robert Brown discovered the nucleus (1831).
**Cell theory:** all plants and animals are made of cells, and all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

table: Small; nuclear region (nucleoid) with no nuclear membrane
Larger; nucleus with a nuclear membrane
More than one chromosome; membrane-bound organelles present
Selectively permeable; lets only some substances in and out
Made of cellulose; gives strength and lets the cell survive in dilute solutions
Contains chromosomes (DNA); controls the cell's activities
Rough ER (with ribosomes) makes proteins; smooth ER makes fats; transport channels; detoxification
Stores, modifies and packages products; forms lysosomes
Digest foreign material and worn-out parts; 'suicide bags' of the cell
Release energy as ATP; 'powerhouse'; have their own DNA and ribosomes
Store materials; very large in plant cells, small in animal cells

box: **Osmosis:** water moves through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a concentrated one.

Cell in a **hypotonic** (dilute) solution swells · **isotonic**: no change · **hypertonic** (concentrated): shrinks. Plasmolysis: a plant cell's contents shrink away from the wall when it loses water.

blocks.p: 1. Why are lysosomes called the 'suicide bags' of the cell?
2. What happens to a raisin placed in plain water, and why?
